1	# Gift cards
2	
3	Customers can buy a gift card for any amount and give the code to someone else.
4	
5	- Customers buy a gift card for any amount and receive a code.
6	- Gift cards never expire.
7	- The buyer receives the card code by email after purchase.
8	- Balances are integer cents (ADR-0002).
9	- Partial redemption is allowed; the remainder stays on the card.
10	- Remove the legacy coupon module.
11	- Out of scope: bulk issuance for corporate customers.
12

1	# 0001. Idempotency keys
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	The payment provider retries webhook delivery on timeout or non-2xx
6	responses. Without a stable way to recognize a retry, a redelivered webhook
7	for an event we already processed would be treated as new work, and could
8	produce a second charge for the same subscription period.
9	
10	## Decision
11	
12	A charge's idempotency key is derived from the payment provider's event ID.
13	It MUST NOT be regenerated between retry attempts. Two attempts at the same
14	event are the same charge, never two charges.
15	
16	## Consequences
17	
18	- The `charges` table (via `processed_events`) enforces a unique constraint
19	  on the provider event ID, so a duplicate delivery is rejected at the
20	  database level, not just in application logic.
21	- Handlers must extract the event ID before doing anything else, and use it
22	  as the sole basis for deciding whether a charge already exists.
23	- Idempotency keys are never generated from timestamps, request IDs, or
24	  other values that change between retries of the same event.
25

1	# 0002. Money is integer cents
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Floating-point arithmetic cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly.
6	Billing amounts that pass through float addition, multiplication, or
7	serialization accumulate rounding error, which is unacceptable when the
8	numbers represent money owed or charged to a customer.
9	
10	## Decision
11	
12	All monetary amounts are integer cents. Floats never touch money.
13	
14	## Consequences
15	
16	- Every money column in the database is `BIGINT`, storing cents.
17	- Every money field in application models (e.g. `Plan.amount`) is typed as
18	  an integer, never `float` or `Decimal` derived from a float.
19	- Formatting an amount for display (e.g. `$12.00`) happens only at the
20	  presentation edge, and only by dividing the integer cent value — the
21	  stored and transmitted value is always the integer.
22	- API request and response bodies carry amounts as integers, not decimal
23	  strings or floats.
24

1	# 0003. Retry policy
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Webhook processing can fail transiently (network errors, provider outages,
6	temporary database unavailability). Retrying gives transient failures a
7	chance to succeed, but unbounded retries can mask permanent failures and
8	retries must never be allowed to create duplicate financial records.
9	
10	## Decision
11	
12	Webhook processing retries at most 5 times with exponential backoff. A retry
13	MUST NOT create a new charge.
14	
15	## Consequences
16	
17	- The worker tracks attempt count per event and stops retrying after 5
18	  attempts, surfacing the event as failed for manual investigation.
19	- Backoff between attempts grows exponentially, to avoid hammering a
20	  degraded payment provider or database.
21	- Because retries reuse the same idempotency key (ADR-0001), a retry that
22	  reaches an already-created charge updates or attempts that charge — it
23	  never inserts a second one.
24

1	# 0004. Handlers enqueue only
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	HTTP handlers run inline with the request/response cycle and are subject to
6	client timeouts. The payment provider's API can be slow or unavailable.
7	Calling it directly from a handler ties request latency to an external
8	service and makes retries (ADR-0003) harder to reason about, since a
9	handler that times out mid-call leaves the caller unsure whether the call
10	happened.
11	
12	## Decision
13	
14	HTTP handlers validate and enqueue. Only the worker talks to the payment
15	provider.
16	
17	## Consequences
18	
19	- Handlers are limited to: validating the request, writing/updating rows
20	  that represent intent (e.g. a pending charge or a queued event), and
21	  returning a response. They perform no outbound calls to the payment
22	  provider.
23	- All communication with the payment provider — charging, confirming,
24	  refunding — happens in the worker process, which owns retry and backoff
25	  behavior.
26	- This keeps handler latency bounded by the database, not by a third party.
27

1	# 0005. Prepaid balances expire after twelve months
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Any prepaid balance a customer holds against Orbit — account credit,
6	promotional credit, and future stored-value products — is a liability on
7	the books until it is spent. Finance asked for a bound on how long that
8	liability can stay open, so year-end reconciliation has a horizon.
9	
10	## Decision
11	
12	Prepaid balances expire twelve months after the day they were funded.
13	Expired balance is written off; it is never refunded or extended.
14	
15	## Consequences
16	
17	- Every table that stores a prepaid balance carries an `expires_at`
18	  timestamp, set at funding time to funding time plus twelve months.
19	- Redemption paths refuse an expired balance with an explicit error rather
20	  than silently treating it as zero.
21	- A product that needs a different horizon must supersede this ADR, not
22	  special-case it.
23

1	# Orbit — Domain Language
2	
3	This repo is the [Hervé](https://app.herve.review) demo: every line was
4	written by an AI agent, guided by this document and the ADRs it links to.
5	
6	Orbit is a subscription billing API. This document defines the vocabulary used
7	throughout the code, docs, and commit messages. Use these terms precisely.
8	
9	- **Plan** — a named price point. Has an amount (integer cents) and an
10	  interval (`monthly` or `yearly`). Plans do not change once subscriptions
11	  reference them; a price change is a new plan.
12	
13	- **Customer** — someone who can hold subscriptions.
14	
15	- **Subscription** — a customer on a plan, with a current period (start and
16	  end). A subscription produces one charge per period.
17	
18	- **Charge** — one unit of money owed for one subscription period. States:
19	  `pending` → `succeeded` | `failed`. A charge is created once per period and
20	  is never duplicated by retries (see ADR-0001).
21	
22	- **Attempt** — one try at settling a charge. A charge may have many
23	  attempts; an attempt belongs to exactly one charge.
24	
25	- **Event** — an inbound webhook from the payment provider, reporting the
26	  outcome of an attempt to charge a customer.
27	
28	See `docs/adr/` for the rules that govern how these concepts interact.
29

18	CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
19	    id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
20	    customer_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id),
21	    plan_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES plans (id),
22	    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('active', 'canceled')),
23	    current_period_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
24	    current_period_end TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,

32	-- the payment provider's event ID and MUST NOT be regenerated between retry
33	-- attempts (ADR-0001): two attempts at the same event are the same charge.
34	CREATE TABLE charges (
35	    id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
36	    subscription_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES subscriptions (id),
37	    amount_cents BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (amount_cents >= 0),
38	    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'succeeded', 'failed')),
39	    idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
40	    period_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,

43	    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
44	    CHECK (period_end > period_start)
45	);

48	
49	-- One try at settling a charge. A charge may have many attempts.
50	CREATE TABLE attempts (
51	    id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
52	    charge_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES charges (id),
53	    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'succeeded', 'failed')),
54	    provider_reference TEXT,
55	    error_message TEXT,
56	    attempted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
57	);

62	-- provider_event_id is what makes ADR-0001 enforceable at the database
63	-- level: a redelivered webhook for an already-processed event is rejected

"""HTTP routes. Per ADR-0004, handlers validate and enqueue only."""

import logging
import os
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
from typing import Annotated

import asyncpg
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError

from orbit.billing import dead_letter, metrics
from orbit.billing.subscriptions import (
    PlanNotFoundError,
    SubscriptionNotFoundError,
    change_subscription_plan,
)
from orbit.billing.webhooks import InvalidWebhookSignatureError, extract_webhook_ids
from orbit.billing.worker import RetriesExhaustedError, process_webhook_with_retry
from orbit.db import get_connection

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

router = APIRouter()

_SIGNATURE_HEADER = "X-Provider-Signature"


@router.post("/webhooks/provider", status_code=202)
async def receive_provider_webhook(
    request: Request,
    conn: Annotated[asyncpg.Connection, Depends(get_connection)],
) -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Accept a payment-provider webhook delivery.

    Verifies the signature, then validates and enqueues per ADR-0004 — this
    handler makes no outbound calls to the payment provider. This is the
    receipt stage of the webhook pipeline; see `process_webhook_with_retry`
    for retry/backoff and `orbit.billing.webhooks.receive_webhook` for
    validation and settlement.
    """
    signature = request.headers.get(_SIGNATURE_HEADER)
    if signature is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"missing {_SIGNATURE_HEADER} header")

    secret = os.environ["PROVIDER_WEBHOOK_SECRET"]
    payload = await request.body()
    ids = extract_webhook_ids(payload)
    logger.info("webhook %s (delivery %s): received", ids.event_id, ids.delivery_id)

    try:
        await process_webhook_with_retry(conn, payload=payload, signature=signature, secret=secret)
    except InvalidWebhookSignatureError as exc:
        logger.warning("webhook %s (delivery %s): invalid signature", ids.event_id, ids.delivery_id)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="invalid signature") from exc
    except ValidationError as exc:
        logger.warning("webhook %s (delivery %s): malformed payload", ids.event_id, ids.delivery_id)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="malformed webhook payload") from exc
    except RetriesExhaustedError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail="webhook processing failed") from exc

    return {"received": True}


class DeadLetterEntry(BaseModel):
    id: int
    provider_event_id: str
    delivery_id: str
    payload: dict[str, object]
    error_message: str
    attempts: int
    failed_at: datetime


@router.get("/webhooks/dead-letter")
async def list_webhook_dead_letters(
    conn: Annotated[asyncpg.Connection, Depends(get_connection)],
) -> list[DeadLetterEntry]:
    """List webhook deliveries that exhausted all retry attempts, most recent first.

    Lets support see what got dropped without digging through logs.
    """
    entries = await dead_letter.list_dead_letters(conn)
    return [
        DeadLetterEntry(
            id=entry.id,
            provider_event_id=entry.provider_event_id,
            delivery_id=entry.delivery_id,
            payload=entry.payload,
            error_message=entry.error_message,
            attempts=entry.attempts,
            failed_at=entry.failed_at,
        )
        for entry in entries
    ]


class ChargeOutcomeCounts(BaseModel):
    day: date
    succeeded: int
    failed: int


@router.get("/metrics/charges")
async def get_charge_metrics(
    conn: Annotated[asyncpg.Connection, Depends(get_connection)],
) -> list[ChargeOutcomeCounts]:
    """Charge outcome counts by day (succeeded vs failed), most recent day first."""
    daily_counts = await metrics.list_charge_outcomes_by_day(conn)
    return [
        ChargeOutcomeCounts(day=d.day, succeeded=d.succeeded, failed=d.failed) for d in daily_counts
    ]


class ChangePlanRequest(BaseModel):
    plan_id: int


class ChangePlanResponse(BaseModel):
    subscription_id: int
    previous_plan_id: int
    new_plan_id: int
    prorated_amount_cents: int


@router.post("/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/plan")
async def change_subscription_plan_route(
    subscription_id: int,
    body: ChangePlanRequest,
    conn: Annotated[asyncpg.Connection, Depends(get_connection)],
) -> ChangePlanResponse:
    """Change a subscription's plan, returning the prorated amount owed or credited.

    `prorated_amount_cents` follows the sign convention of
    `prorated_amount_cents()` in `orbit.billing.proration`: positive means
    the customer owes the difference, negative means they're credited.
    """
    try:
        result = await change_subscription_plan(
            conn,
            subscription_id=subscription_id,
            new_plan_id=body.plan_id,
            changed_at=datetime.now(UTC),
        )
    except SubscriptionNotFoundError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="subscription not found") from exc
    except PlanNotFoundError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="plan not found") from exc

    return ChangePlanResponse(
        subscription_id=result.subscription_id,
        previous_plan_id=result.previous_plan_id,
        new_plan_id=result.new_plan_id,
        prorated_amount_cents=result.prorated_amount_cents,
    )

1	"""Dead-letter storage for webhook events that exhaust all retry attempts (ADR-0003).
2	
3	This is the terminal sink `process_webhook_with_retry` writes to instead of
4	letting a permanently-failing delivery vanish after its last log line — see
5	`orbit.billing.worker.process_webhook_with_retry`.
6	"""
7	
8	import json
9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	from datetime import datetime
11	
12	import asyncpg
13	
14	
15	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
16	class DeadLetter:
17	    """One webhook delivery that failed on every retry attempt."""
18	
19	    id: int
20	    provider_event_id: str
21	    delivery_id: str
22	    payload: dict[str, object]
23	    error_message: str
24	    attempts: int
25	    failed_at: datetime
26	
27	
28	async def record_dead_letter(  # noqa: PLR0913 -- one field per dead-letter column
29	    conn: asyncpg.Connection,
30	    *,
31	    provider_event_id: str,
32	    delivery_id: str,
33	    payload: bytes,
34	    error_message: str,
35	    attempts: int,
36	) -> None:
37	    """Persist a webhook delivery that exhausted all retry attempts.
38	
39	    `payload` is the raw request body; by the time retries are exhausted it
40	    has already round-tripped through `WebhookEvent.model_validate_json` at
41	    least once (only transient DB/network errors are retried — see
42	    `orbit.billing.worker._RETRYABLE_ERRORS`), so it is expected to be valid
43	    JSON. It is decoded defensively anyway since this is a last-resort sink
44	    that must not itself raise and mask the real failure.
45	    """
46	    try:

content.text:
I've read the PRD, all five ADRs, and the existing schema/model/test patterns. Before I finalize a plan, there's a real conflict I need you to resolve:

**PRD** (`docs/prd/gift-cards.md`) says: *"Gift cards never expire."*

**ADR-0005** (merged just before this task, PR #17) says: *"Any prepaid balance a customer holds against Orbit — account credit, promotional credit, **and future stored-value products** — is a liability... Prepaid balances expire twelve months after the day they were funded... A product that needs a different horizon must supersede this ADR, not special-case it."*

Gift cards are explicitly the "future stored-value product" this ADR anticipated (the README even calls gift cards "prepaid balances redeemable at checkout"), and the `gift_cards` table would need an `expires_at` column per ADR-0005's own consequence clause. But the PRD directly contradicts that. This isn't something I should silently resolve by picking one side — it changes the schema (whether `expires_at` exists) and it's a governance question (ADR-0005 says a differing product must *supersede* it, not quietly ignore it).

Two reasonable paths:

1. **Write ADR-0006** that explicitly supersedes ADR-0005 for gift cards ("gift cards do not expire — see ADR-0006"), and build the table without `expires_at`. This follows the PRD and follows ADR-0005's own governance rule for how to deviate from it.
2. **Follow ADR-0005 as-is**: gift cards expire 12 months after funding, add `expires_at`, and treat the PRD's "never expire" line as stale/wrong — flag it back to whoever wrote the PRD rather than build it as written.

I'd lean toward (1) — the ADR itself hands you the escape hatch, and PRDs should generally win over an ADR when they genuinely conflict, as long as the deviation is recorded. But this is a product/compliance call (finance asked for the 12-month bound), so I want your call before I bake it into the schema. Which do you want?

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle — consult them before and during the loop, not after.

When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification — "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists — and survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams — where tests go

A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything — agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?"

## Anti-patterns

- **Implementation-coupled** — mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological** — the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth — a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing** — writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead — one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

-- Prepaid balances customers buy and redeem at checkout (docs/prd/gift-cards.md).
-- Amounts are BIGINT cents (ADR-0002). Expires twelve months after funding,
-- written off rather than refunded or extended, per ADR-0005.
CREATE TABLE gift_cards (
    id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    purchaser_customer_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id),
    initial_amount_cents BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (initial_amount_cents >= 0),
    balance_cents BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (balance_cents >= 0),
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    CHECK (balance_cents <= initial_amount_cents),
    CHECK (expires_at > created_at)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_gift_cards_purchaser_customer_id ON gift_cards (purchaser_customer_id);
